messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: `pd_queue_backpressure` on metrics-ingest-cluster (severity: P1)

incident-bot: Alert details:
```
alert: pd_queue_backpressure
expr: sum(rate(log_ingest_queue_size[1m])) by (cluster) > 5000
labels: cluster=metrics-ingest-cluster, team=eng-sre
annotations:
  summary: "Log ingest queue backlog increasing >5k/min"
  runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/log-ingest-backpressure
```

alex: acked in PD, I'm looking at queues now. grabbing offsets and consumer lag.

pagerbot: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged by alex (30s ago) :thumbsup:

maria: alex can you confirm whether this is producer-side spike or downstream Kafka consumer stall? any customer-facing errors?

alex: quick check: kafka.consumer_lag for ingress-consumers jumped from ~100 to ~15k in last 5m. running `kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group ingress-consumers` now.

jon: seeing scrape errors too — prometheus scrape job `nodes-exporter` for region-eu dropped ~40% of targets around the same time. logs show connection reset when scraping some ec2 hosts. not sure if related.

alex: pasted consumer-groups output: ```
GROUP           TOPIC           PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG     CONSUMER-ID
ingress-consumers ingest-logs     0          1250000         1265000         15000  consumer-12
ingress-consumers ingest-logs     1          1248000         1263000         15000  consumer-7
```

tess: @alex quick try: bounce ingress-consumers pods one-by-one to let them rebalance, but keep replication factor in mind. also increase consumer parallelism if pods are CPU starved.

alex: running `kubectl rollout restart deployment/ingress-consumers -n metrics-prod --grace-period=60` on a single AZ now (handful of pods). will watch lag.

maria: also flagging possible disk io saturation on brokers — iostat on broker-3 shows avgqu-sz spiking. if brokers blocked, consumers will pile up even after restarts. jon can you check broker metrics?

jon: checking broker metrics: `kafka_server_broker_topic_metrics_messages_in_total` is normal, but `kafka_server_replica_fetch_manager` shows replication_fetch_time_ms high on broker-3. suspect EBS throttling. opening cloudwatch quick view.

incident-bot: PD escalation policy will run at +10m if no update. current status: acknowledged by alex.

alex: first restarted pod came up, consumer lag dropped from 15k -> 6k on partition 0, others similar. good sign. continuing rolling restarts slowly.

pagerbot: Autopage note: incident-bot detected correlated alerts: `prom_scrape_error_rate` and `kafka_replica_fetch_time_ms` — linking for triage.

maria: customer impact check: logs show a few 503s in the API ingress when log processing backlog crossed threshold about 12m ago. small subset of customers saw delayed event availability (mostly bulk ingest). notifying customer-ops.

alex: added temporary throttle on non-critical producers via kafka topic-level throttle: `kafka-configs --alter --entity-type topics --entity-name ingest-logs --add-config retention.ms=...` (we used producer-side backpressure knob) — will revert after stable.

tess: any possibility this started from a deploy? recent infra deploys? @sre-rotation do you recall a deploy around 4142509900?

sre-rotation: deploy-bot shows no infra deploys in that minute, there was a small model-serving rollout earlier but unrelated.

jon: broker-3 EBS showed ~8s avg latency in CloudWatch — opened support ticket with cloud provider and moved partitions away from broker-3: `kafka-reassign-partitions` plan submitted.

alex: consumer lag now down to ~500-1k after second pod restart and partition reassignment in progress. processing throughput improving.

maria: creating incident doc: https://redwood-internal/incidents/4142509999 - adding timeline and customer impact notes. tagging @customer-ops.

incident-bot: Reminder: runbook step 3 suggests enabling consumer parallelism and triggering partition reassignment if lag doesn't drop below 2k in 15m.

alex: noted, continuing ramp — will keep updates here. if lag doesn't fully resolve in 20m we escalate to infra oncall.

pagerbot: PagerDuty: escalation scheduled at 4142510599 if no resolution.

jon: followups for postmortem: 1) why EBS burst credits exhausted on broker-3; 2) scrape error root cause — some nodes had iptables conntrack exhaustion around same window, could be a networking hit. collecting kernel logs.

tess: good mitigation sequence. when stable, can we add a Prometheus alert that correlates broker EBS latency + consumer lag to reduce manual triage time?

maria: ++. also add a dashboard panel for cross-correlation (kafka lag vs ebs latency vs prom_scrape_errors).

alex: incident update: consumer lag <800 for all partitions, broker reassign in progress, cloud support acknowledged health check > investigating I/O. marking this as stabilizing.

sre-rotation: taking over monitoring for the next 30m, will post any regressions here. thanks team. :heart:

maria: noted. customer-ops alerted, minimal customer impact but tracking for SLA. closing PD when fully resolved.

incident-bot: Incident status: stabilizing -> monitor. PD will auto-close on resolve if no further pages.

alex: final note before handoff: added temporary autoscaling policy for ingress-consumers to better handle spikes (min pods -> +2) and filed follow-up ticket to revisit broker instance types.

tess: thanks all, good ops.
